GEKCO SLAPP Suit

By: Stenette Grosskopf | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Slapped with a R197million lawsuit, simply for for exercising their democratic right to speak out against development

Unique Selling Point:
Gekco - the Greater Kyalami Conservancy and their chairperson, Kristin Kallesen - have been slapped with a R197 million lawsuit by Century Property Developments and Riversand Developments for the income they have allegedly lost because of her continuous objections against their developments in the Kyalami area. This has been labellled as a SLAPP (Strategic Lawsuits against Public Participation) lawsuit... a scare tactic originating from the States and used to scare activists from opposing big corporates... in this case from development.

Summary:
A R197 million lawsuit by Century Property Developments and Riversand Developments has been filed against GEKCO and their chairperson in her personal capacity. The developers claim that she and her Conservancy have caused them massive loss of income. Especially in a country like South Africa, environmental activism and public participation are essential to keep irresponsible development in check. No-one is saying there should not be any development, but we know that government is not ticking all the boxes when it comes to monitoring things like EIAs and other development regulations. Silencing those looking out for the environment could be disastrous in the long run. And the irony is many developers use the “unspoilt nature”-card to sell their housing estates, while they are effectively decimating nature in the process.

Century Property Developments claim that none of GECKO's objections throughout the years have been upheld by COJ, and although Kallesen refutes this claim, one can ask the question.. "How effective is the public participation process, especially if objectors can easily be silenced?"

Further information:
Gekco is a peri-urban conservancy located in the heart of Gauteng between Pretoria and Johannesburg. It is characterised by grasslands and wetlands and a high level of biodiversity. The large open spaces promote a healthy outdoor lifestyle which has attracted many horse riders and equestrian businesses as well as mountain bikers and nature enthusiasts. They are registered with the Gauteng Conservancy Association and with the National Association of Conservancies of South Africa and is recognised by the City of Joburg. The Conservancy is all about protecting nature with projects to safeguard the grasslands, wetlands, bullfrogs and hedgehogs and grass owls, to name but a few… They promote the idea of living in harmony with nature, as opposed to sterile eco-lifestyle estates. However, since 2009 Riverside farm ha steadily been developed by Century Property Developments and Riverside Developments. The Diepsloot Business Hub was built to essentially uplift the township community and is continuously expanding. The entire area is slowly being redeveloped into a light industrial zone - which the residents feel has a huge impact on the area. For the past decade Gecko has been opposing these developments vehemently, keeping check on EIA’s and regularly lodging complaints against infringements by the developers…

But there are other controversies around Century Property Development. In 2019 they were involved in a building scandal of UJ residences adjacent to Campus Square in Auckland Park. The COJ Building Building Control Officer was dismissed after an internal disciplinary found him to be guilty of gross negligence. There were issues with Building plans submission fees not being paid. And a private objector, who wants to remain anonymous, was eventually sued for R5million by Century. No-one knows for sure but I think she settled eventually and refuses to speak about the incident. BUT... a couple of weeks ago a student fell from the first floor basketball court and died. It has been said that that court was not on the original plans approved by the city.

In 2010, a similar lawsuit was brought against Helen Duigan for opposing a housing development on the fringes of the Renosterspruit Conservancy. The 330-house luxury estate was eventually built, the developer sued her and three others for R170 million. The case made headlines when the court ruled in their favour, because "you can’t simply sue people for exercising their democratic right to speak out against development”

In Feb 2021 the high court in Cape Town held that a series of defamation lawsuits totalling R14.25-million brought by Australian mining company Mineral Commodities Ltd (MRC) and its local subsidiary, Mineral Sands Resources, against three environmental lawyers, two activists and a social worker who criticised its operations is an abuse of legal process. A precedent was set. Western Cape high court Deputy Judge President Patricia Goliath said “In essence, SLAPPs are designed to turn the justice system into a weapon to intimidate people who are exercising their constitutional rights, restrain public interest in advocacy and activism and convert matters of public interest into technical private law disputes.”

SLAPP suits is that it is a way for big wealthy corporates to silence the small guys. They have the money to drag out litigation in court and to effectively silence environmental activists who often don’t have the resources to fight them.

Script:


GEKCO SLAPP SCRIPT MASTER

V/O
Kyalami resident and keen environmentalist, Kristin Kallessen is no stranger to the law... For over a decade she has been devoting her time to protecting a 4000ha conservancy on the outskirts of Joburg.
Kristin
This is very unique in that we’re literally on the edge of Johannesburg with built-up areas all around us. And there’s this tranquil slice of paradise here.
V/O
As chair of GEKCO -- the Greater Kyalami Conservancy -- Kallessen has been taking on the City of Joburg and big corporate developers, fearlessly defending the conservancy’s unique biodiversity, and the residents’ peaceful and somewhat idyllic existence.
Kristin
I don’t know if anyone can stop the development and that’s not necessarily the conservancy’s aim, but we want to make sure that development protects the environment no matter what happens.
LINK
It’s a familiar story. A piece of land with some combination of significant habitat and species that have coexisted for thousands of years. A developer enters and earmarks it for something that we as humans need -- a shopping mall, a housing estate… and the battle lines are drawn!
V/O
Conserving land ideally located between Gauteng’s two major economic hubs comes with difficulties... but in February this year Kallessen was met with one of the biggest challenges of her life… A 197 million rand lawsuit.
Kristin
It's been extremely stressful. It's been very time consuming to have to deal with this.

DEREK: Kristin, explain the lawsuit to us, what does it say?

It basically sues me and my personal and it was personal capacity as well as the conservancy to reclaim alleged damages for delays due to the objections that were lodged during the public participation process.
V/O
The lawsuit has been brought by Century Property Developments and Riversands Developments, both owned by property development mogul, Mark Corbett, who has been driving development in the area since the late 2000’s.
Mark Corbett
The intention is to join Johannesburg with Diepsloot and create economic activity and upliftment for everybody.
V/O
But this lawsuit against Kallessen and GEKCO is argued to be a potential SLAPP -- Strategic Litigation Against Public Participation…
Divina Naidoo
It is a means that is used usually by big large corporate entities that are wanting to silence and or exhaust finances for smaller public interest groups.
V/O
Schindlers’ Attorneys associate, Divina Naidoo specialises in environmental law and says she is increasingly dealing with this ‘US-Style corporate hardball’-strategy.
Divina Naidoo
If you are not backed by a larger organization with significant funding, you may find yourself in a precarious position because litigation is quite expensive.
V/O
For Kallessen there is no doubt that the R197million lawsuit is intended to intimidate her and other objectors...
Kristin
We're being sued due to the alleged delays, but at the same time, it does feel like a bullying tactic and we have argued that in our papers.
V/O
In addition to the exorbitant amount being claimed, the imbalance of power is often a characteristic of a SLAPP suit, explains independent advocate Ben Winks.
Ben Winks
Where you're seeing an example of corporate bullying or even political bullying, a David and Goliath kind of scenario, that is one of the hallmarks of a SLAPP.
V/O
But Corbett says his aim is not to deter Kallessen or the Conservancy from the public participation process....
Mark Corbett
DEREK: Now it has been labeled as a SLAPP litigation. Do you agree with that?

I think it's an incorrect term for this because with the court case we’re basically looking for clarification on two issues with the court case. Is GEKCO in fact bound by their constitution, which specifically excludes Riversands from their area. And the second is, can they expand their conservancy without council’s consent into an area that is earmarked for development...
V/O
Understandably, Kallessen is wary of discussing the elements of the lawsuit.
Kristin Kallesen
We expect that the issues will be fully ventilated in court during the course of the proceedings so we won’t be discussing that at this time...
V/O
The battle between Century Property Developments and GEKCO spans over a decade. According to Corbett the ongoing dispute pertains to the development of a buffer zone between the Diepsloot township and The Conservancy….
Mark Corbett
Riversands at present is only about 15 percent developed. But if it wasn't for GEKCO imagine we would be. You know, I think it would be close to 70, 80 percent developed.
V/O
But Kallessen says they cannot simply let rampant development forge ahead...
Kristin Kallessen
Kristen, what development projects have you objected to in the past and why?

We've objected to shopping centers. We've objected to high density residential developments, light industrial commercial type developments because they're not fitting with what this area has to offer and they would be better located closer to the city.


LINK
Kyalami is perhaps best known for the grand prix’s of the 70’s and 80’s and of course the horses. According to a survey over 330 properties in the area are somehow linked to the equestrian industry.
V/o
And it is this so-called elitist lifestyle that the conservancy aims to protect, alleges Corbett.
Mark Corbett
I think it's the normal thing that residents are scared of change. You know, I think a very kind of pro in protecting the elitist lifestyle and the equestrian lifestyle. And they're very scared of traffic generated that may arrive in the area.
Kristin Kallessen
DEREK: Do you think developers and other people might say that that's an elitist view?

Basically, I think everyone has a right to live how they're able to. But also this is the home to the equestrian sport in South Africa. And that also is an important industry.
V/O
Development -- even on the boundary of the Conservancy -- will have significant impacts, says Kallessen.
Kristin
If you've got a high density shopping center, for example, you need to bring services into supply that such as sewage, such as roads, that has a knock on impact on the environment.
Anton van Niekerk
We’ve got something called Egoli Granite Grassland which is unique to the Gauteng area. We’ve also got mixed bushveld as well as wetlands.
V/O
Anton van Niekerk manages the biodiversity programme within the GEKCO conservancy, which is also home to elusive species like the endangered African grass owl... and the giant bullfrog...
Anton van Niekerk
What we have seen in other areas is that with the reducing of space, reducing of access to water and access to feeding … the wildlife definitely does move out, for sure.
V/O
My meeting with Corbett included a detailed briefing session of the development done thus far on the farm, Riversands. This includes light industrial, commercial and a low-income housing estate with 2,000 units. But continued delays have been costly, says Corbett.
Mark Corbett
You must understand that significant damage is done with their objections. You look at a development like this, what impact it could have on Diepsloot and the possible jobs it could create and the people who could change their lives and with GEKCO to sit in their homes and object and stop every development also has vast implications.

DEREK: 197 million rands may not be a scary amount to you, but for the average Joe, this is huge.

You know, it is it's a significant amount of money. Derek the figure of 197 million is very symbolic because that is the value of the economic activity that's been removed in this area.
Melany Cottrill
My experience with Century is that they wouldn't go that route if things weren't dire. But the extraordinary costs of spurious objections is huge.
V/O
Estate Agent and property developer, Melany Cotrill sympathises with Corbett’s predicament, understanding the financial implications of delays.
Melany Cottrill
DEREK: According to the law, as citizens have a right to object to developments that you agree with that?

I completely agree, but there must be some accountability. What we need is to differentiate between public opinion and public interest. And where there’s an objection that’s spurious, for example, the city needs a mechanism to identify that. What is the goal of the object? If it is just to delay? We need a mechanism to put a stop to that because we just cannot afford the economic bleed in our country.
V/O
But the big question for Kallessen is: “why should she be penalised for simply exercising her constitutional rights as part of the public participation process?”…
Kristin Kallessen
00:08:04:05 - 00:08:08:00
So what would you say is unfair about this lawsuit?

00:08:08:24 - 00:08:21:09
Well, firstly, they're asking for two hundred million rand, none of which any of us have.
Ben Winks
It's unrealistic to expect, you know, ordinary citizens to be able to put up that kind of money… , and often these suits are brought with the knowledge that that kind of person won't have the money even to defend it, even to put up a proper defense that what they're saying is justifiable. The amount of damages is not realistically recoverable. And where that's the case, that can be a factor that the court will take into account in determining that it's a slap or an abuse of process.


V/O
Unlike in the United States, South Africa has no legislation to deal with SLAPP.
Ben Winks
The position in South Africa is that you still have to defend yourself. In order for the court to protect you from a SLAPP you have to convince the court that it is a SLAPP.
V/O
And while Corbett is eager to proceed with his developments, Kallessen and GEKCO are preparing their defense... But it could be years before they know for certain what the future holds.
Kristin Kallessen
DEREK: So has it come as a surprise or shock that objecting to development can come at such a personal cost?

It it is a shock, but it's also extremely unfortunate because everyone has the right to do this regardless of where you live. And that's why you have public participation in the first place. And to deny that public participation is actually to deny somebody's rights to expression. And that's really not acceptable.




END


PROMO 1 11”
A non-profit conservancy north of Johannesburg is being sued for almost two hundred million rand by a corporate developer... after a years-long battle over development in the area.


PROMO 2 21”
A big corporate developer is seeking almost two hundred million rand from an environmentalist and her conservancy for objecting to his developments.

It's unrealistic to expect, you know, ordinary citizens to be able to put up that kind of money,

But is this a justified claim or an intimidation tactic aimed at silencing its critics?


PROMO 3 21”
What does it take to protect a peri-urban conservancy on the outskirts of Joburg? Time, dedication… and maybe even a hundred and ninety seven million rand!

UPSOUND: We're being sued due to the alleged delays, but at the same time, it does feel like a bullying tactic

Environmentalists vs Corporate Developers… we investigate what’s at stake.

2021 - Carte Blanche HD nombuso@carteblanche.co.za 20 August 2021 Script: GEKCO SLAPP SCRIPT MASTER V/O Kyalami resident and keen environmentalist, Kristin Kallessen is no stranger to the law... For over a decade she has been devoting her time to protecting a 4000ha conservancy on the outskirts of Joburg. Kristin This is very unique in that we’re literally on the edge of Johannesburg with built-up areas all around us. And there’s this tranquil slice of paradise here. V/O As chair of GEKCO -- the Greater Kyalami Conservancy -- Kallessen has been taking on the City of Joburg and big corporate developers, fearlessly defending the conservancy’s unique biodiversity, and the residents’ peaceful and somewhat idyllic existence. Kristin I don’t know if anyone can stop the development and that’s not necessarily the conservancy’s aim, but we want to make sure that development protects the environment no matter what happens. LINK It’s a familiar story. A piece of land with some combination of significant habitat and species that have coexisted for thousands of years. A developer enters and earmarks it for something that we as humans need -- a shopping mall, a housing estate… and the battle lines are drawn! V/O Conserving land ideally located between Gauteng’s two major economic hubs comes with difficulties... but in February this year Kallessen was met with one of the biggest challenges of her life… A 197 million rand lawsuit. Kristin It's been extremely stressful. It's been very time consuming to have to deal with this. DEREK: Kristin, explain the lawsuit to us, what does it say? It basically sues me and my personal and it was personal capacity as well as the conservancy to reclaim alleged damages for delays due to the objections that were lodged during the public participation process. V/O The lawsuit has been brought by Century Property Developments and Riversands Developments, both owned by property development mogul, Mark Corbett, who has been driving development in the area since the late 2000’s. Mark Corbett The intention is to join Johannesburg with Diepsloot and create economic activity and upliftment for everybody. V/O But this lawsuit against Kallessen and GEKCO is argued to be a potential SLAPP -- Strategic Litigation Against Public Participation… Divina Naidoo It is a means that is used usually by big large corporate entities that are wanting to silence and or exhaust finances for smaller public interest groups. V/O Schindlers’ Attorneys associate, Divina Naidoo specialises in environmental law and says she is increasingly dealing with this ‘US-Style corporate hardball’-strategy. Divina Naidoo If you are not backed by a larger organization with significant funding, you may find yourself in a precarious position because litigation is quite expensive. V/O For Kallessen there is no doubt that the R197million lawsuit is intended to intimidate her and other objectors... Kristin We're being sued due to the alleged delays, but at the same time, it does feel like a bullying tactic and we have argued that in our papers. V/O In addition to the exorbitant amount being claimed, the imbalance of power is often a characteristic of a SLAPP suit, explains independent advocate Ben Winks. Ben Winks Where you're seeing an example of corporate bullying or even political bullying, a David and Goliath kind of scenario, that is one of the hallmarks of a SLAPP. V/O But Corbett says his aim is not to deter Kallessen or the Conservancy from the public participation process.... Mark Corbett DEREK: Now it has been labeled as a SLAPP litigation. Do you agree with that? I think it's an incorrect term for this because with the court case we’re basically looking for clarification on two issues with the court case. Is GEKCO in fact bound by their constitution, which specifically excludes Riversands from their area. And the second is, can they expand their conservancy without council’s consent into an area that is earmarked for development... V/O Understandably, Kallessen is wary of discussing the elements of the lawsuit. Kristin Kallesen We expect that the issues will be fully ventilated in court during the course of the proceedings so we won’t be discussing that at this time... V/O The battle between Century Property Developments and GEKCO spans over a decade. According to Corbett the ongoing dispute pertains to the development of a buffer zone between the Diepsloot township and The Conservancy…. Mark Corbett Riversands at present is only about 15 percent developed. But if it wasn't for GEKCO imagine we would be. You know, I think it would be close to 70, 80 percent developed. V/O But Kallessen says they cannot simply let rampant development forge ahead... Kristin Kallessen Kristen, what development projects have you objected to in the past and why? We've objected to shopping centers. We've objected to high density residential developments, light industrial commercial type developments because they're not fitting with what this area has to offer and they would be better located closer to the city. LINK Kyalami is perhaps best known for the grand prix’s of the 70’s and 80’s and of course the horses. According to a survey over 330 properties in the area are somehow linked to the equestrian industry. V/o And it is this so-called elitist lifestyle that the conservancy aims to protect, alleges Corbett. Mark Corbett I think it's the normal thing that residents are scared of change. You know, I think a very kind of pro in protecting the elitist lifestyle and the equestrian lifestyle. And they're very scared of traffic generated that may arrive in the area. Kristin Kallessen DEREK: Do you think developers and other people might say that that's an elitist view? Basically, I think everyone has a right to live how they're able to. But also this is the home to the equestrian sport in South Africa. And that also is an important industry. V/O Development -- even on the boundary of the Conservancy -- will have significant impacts, says Kallessen. Kristin If you've got a high density shopping center, for example, you need to bring services into supply that such as sewage, such as roads, that has a knock on impact on the environment. Anton van Niekerk We’ve got something called Egoli Granite Grassland which is unique to the Gauteng area. We’ve also got mixed bushveld as well as wetlands. V/O Anton van Niekerk manages the biodiversity programme within the GEKCO conservancy, which is also home to elusive species like the endangered African grass owl... and the giant bullfrog... Anton van Niekerk What we have seen in other areas is that with the reducing of space, reducing of access to water and access to feeding … the wildlife definitely does move out, for sure. V/O My meeting with Corbett included a detailed briefing session of the development done thus far on the farm, Riversands. This includes light industrial, commercial and a low-income housing estate with 2,000 units. But continued delays have been costly, says Corbett. Mark Corbett You must understand that significant damage is done with their objections. You look at a development like this, what impact it could have on Diepsloot and the possible jobs it could create and the people who could change their lives and with GEKCO to sit in their homes and object and stop every development also has vast implications. DEREK: 197 million rands may not be a scary amount to you, but for the average Joe, this is huge. You know, it is it's a significant amount of money. Derek the figure of 197 million is very symbolic because that is the value of the economic activity that's been removed in this area. Melany Cottrill My experience with Century is that they wouldn't go that route if things weren't dire. But the extraordinary costs of spurious objections is huge. V/O Estate Agent and property developer, Melany Cotrill sympathises with Corbett’s predicament, understanding the financial implications of delays. Melany Cottrill DEREK: According to the law, as citizens have a right to object to developments that you agree with that? I completely agree, but there must be some accountability. What we need is to differentiate between public opinion and public interest. And where there’s an objection that’s spurious, for example, the city needs a mechanism to identify that. What is the goal of the object? If it is just to delay? We need a mechanism to put a stop to that because we just cannot afford the economic bleed in our country. V/O But the big question for Kallessen is: “why should she be penalised for simply exercising her constitutional rights as part of the public participation process?”… Kristin Kallessen 00:08:04:05 - 00:08:08:00 So what would you say is unfair about this lawsuit? 00:08:08:24 - 00:08:21:09 Well, firstly, they're asking for two hundred million rand, none of which any of us have. Ben Winks It's unrealistic to expect, you know, ordinary citizens to be able to put up that kind of money… , and often these suits are brought with the knowledge that that kind of person won't have the money even to defend it, even to put up a proper defense that what they're saying is justifiable. The amount of damages is not realistically recoverable. And where that's the case, that can be a factor that the court will take into account in determining that it's a slap or an abuse of process. V/O Unlike in the United States, South Africa has no legislation to deal with SLAPP. Ben Winks The position in South Africa is that you still have to defend yourself. In order for the court to protect you from a SLAPP you have to convince the court that it is a SLAPP. V/O And while Corbett is eager to proceed with his developments, Kallessen and GEKCO are preparing their defense... But it could be years before they know for certain what the future holds. Kristin Kallessen DEREK: So has it come as a surprise or shock that objecting to development can come at such a personal cost? It it is a shock, but it's also extremely unfortunate because everyone has the right to do this regardless of where you live. And that's why you have public participation in the first place. And to deny that public participation is actually to deny somebody's rights to expression. And that's really not acceptable. END PROMO 1 11” A non-profit conservancy north of Johannesburg is being sued for almost two hundred million rand by a corporate developer... after a years-long battle over development in the area. PROMO 2 21” A big corporate developer is seeking almost two hundred million rand from an environmentalist and her conservancy for objecting to his developments. It's unrealistic to expect, you know, ordinary citizens to be able to put up that kind of money, But is this a justified claim or an intimidation tactic aimed at silencing its critics? PROMO 3 21” What does it take to protect a peri-urban conservancy on the outskirts of Joburg? Time, dedication… and maybe even a hundred and ninety seven million rand! metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Slapped with a R197million lawsuit, simply for for exercising their democratic right to speak out against development
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Gekco - the Greater Kyalami Conservancy and their chairperson, Kristin Kallesen - have been slapped with a R197 million lawsuit by Century Property Developments and Riversand Developments for the income they have allegedly lost because of her continuous objections against their developments in the Kyalami area. This has been labellled as a SLAPP (Strategic Lawsuits against Public Participation) lawsuit... a scare tactic originating from the States and used to scare activists from opposing big corporates... in this case from development.
metadata.Summary: A R197 million lawsuit by Century Property Developments and Riversand Developments has been filed against GEKCO and their chairperson in her personal capacity. The developers claim that she and her Conservancy have caused them massive loss of income. Especially in a country like South Africa, environmental activism and public participation are essential to keep irresponsible development in check. No-one is saying there should not be any development, but we know that government is not ticking all the boxes when it comes to monitoring things like EIAs and other development regulations. Silencing those looking out for the environment could be disastrous in the long run. And the irony is many developers use the “unspoilt nature”-card to sell their housing estates, while they are effectively decimating nature in the process. Century Property Developments claim that none of GECKO's objections throughout the years have been upheld by COJ, and although Kallesen refutes this claim, one can ask the question.. "How effective is the public participation process, especially if objectors can easily be silenced?"
metadata.Further information: Gekco is a peri-urban conservancy located in the heart of Gauteng between Pretoria and Johannesburg. It is characterised by grasslands and wetlands and a high level of biodiversity. The large open spaces promote a healthy outdoor lifestyle which has attracted many horse riders and equestrian businesses as well as mountain bikers and nature enthusiasts. They are registered with the Gauteng Conservancy Association and with the National Association of Conservancies of South Africa and is recognised by the City of Joburg. The Conservancy is all about protecting nature with projects to safeguard the grasslands, wetlands, bullfrogs and hedgehogs and grass owls, to name but a few… They promote the idea of living in harmony with nature, as opposed to sterile eco-lifestyle estates. However, since 2009 Riverside farm ha steadily been developed by Century Property Developments and Riverside Developments. The Diepsloot Business Hub was built to essentially uplift the township community and is continuously expanding. The entire area is slowly being redeveloped into a light industrial zone - which the residents feel has a huge impact on the area. For the past decade Gecko has been opposing these developments vehemently, keeping check on EIA’s and regularly lodging complaints against infringements by the developers… But there are other controversies around Century Property Development. In 2019 they were involved in a building scandal of UJ residences adjacent to Campus Square in Auckland Park. The COJ Building Building Control Officer was dismissed after an internal disciplinary found him to be guilty of gross negligence. There were issues with Building plans submission fees not being paid. And a private objector, who wants to remain anonymous, was eventually sued for R5million by Century. No-one knows for sure but I think she settled eventually and refuses to speak about the incident. BUT... a couple of weeks ago a student fell from the first floor basketball court and died. It has been said that that court was not on the original plans approved by the city. In 2010, a similar lawsuit was brought against Helen Duigan for opposing a housing development on the fringes of the Renosterspruit Conservancy. The 330-house luxury estate was eventually built, the developer sued her and three others for R170 million. The case made headlines when the court ruled in their favour, because "you can’t simply sue people for exercising their democratic right to speak out against development” In Feb 2021 the high court in Cape Town held that a series of defamation lawsuits totalling R14.25-million brought by Australian mining company Mineral Commodities Ltd (MRC) and its local subsidiary, Mineral Sands Resources, against three environmental lawyers, two activists and a social worker who criticised its operations is an abuse of legal process. A precedent was set. Western Cape high court Deputy Judge President Patricia Goliath said “In essence, SLAPPs are designed to turn the justice system into a weapon to intimidate people who are exercising their constitutional rights, restrain public interest in advocacy and activism and convert matters of public interest into technical private law disputes.” SLAPP suits is that it is a way for big wealthy corporates to silence the small guys. They have the money to drag out litigation in court and to effectively silence environmental activists who often don’t have the resources to fight them.
